finding.claim: delete_file discards the result of require_allowed (is_allowed), so any caller, including an anonymous one, can delete any file by fid.
finding.source: DELETE /files/<fid> with any or no X-Session-User-Verified header (views.py:12 sets g.user to None when absent)

trace.note: require_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') returns a bool that is never read
is_allowed returns False without raising when the grant is missing

finding.guards_checked: acl.py:8-10 ensure_allowed would abort(403) but is not used here; views.py:10-12 before_request only copies a header and does not authenticate; no route decorator or other middleware checks authorization.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. acl.py:4 is_allowed returns a bool and never raises; views.py:18 calls it as a bare statement so the result is discarded; ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10, which would abort(403)) is imported as views.py:3 but never called in delete_file; views.py:10-12 only copies the X-Session-User-Verified header into g.user with no authentication; no auth decorator or other middleware is present.
verdict.reason: delete_file at views.py:18 discards the bool from require_allowed (acl.py:4, which never aborts), so del STORE[fid] at views.py:19 runs for any request, including one where g.user is None from views.py:12, so an anonymous caller can delete any stored file. The one caveat is that the header name suggests an upstream proxy is meant to set it, and that proxy is not in this codebase, so the anonymous-reachability depends on deployment; the code as written has no check.

finding.claim: Identity is read from the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header and trusted for authorization. Exploitable only if the service is reachable without a proxy that verifies and strips this header.
finding.sink: g.user used in authorization checks at views.py:18 and views.py:26 via acl.py:5

trace.note: grants.get(user) keyed on the caller-supplied value

finding.guards_checked: No validation, signature, or stripping of the header in this codebase. Trust depends on an upstream proxy not present in the audited code. Unconfirmed.

verdict.guard_found: acl.py:8-10 ensure_allowed aborts with 403 and is effective on the rename path (views.py:26). acl.py:4-5 is_allowed returns a bool, and views.py:18 calls it as a bare statement with the result discarded, so it is not a guard. No header validation, signature check, or stripping exists in views.py:12.
verdict.reason: The trace lines exist as described (views.py:12 reads the header unvalidated, acl.py:5 keys grants on it), and the anonymous attacker can reach DELETE /files/<fid> because views.py:18 discards the bool from require_allowed and views.py:19 deletes unconditionally, so no check blocks it, even with no header at all. The rename path at views.py:26 is guarded by ensure_allowed (acl.py:9-10), but an attacker who sets X-Session-User-Verified to a granted user (or reaches the service without the upstream proxy the candidate mentions) bypasses it. The candidate's root cause is incomplete: the delete bypass comes from the ignored return value at views.py:18, not from header trust.
